title: Four Lists Sum to Zero
statement:
You are given four lists of numbers, `first`, `second`, `third` and `fourth`, all of the same length `n`. Count the **tuples of positions `(i, j, k, l)`** (each from `0` to `n - 1`) such that

`first[i] + second[j] + third[k] + fourth[l] == 0`.

Tuples with different positions count separately even if the numbers are equal.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100 (all four lists have n numbers)

hints.nudge: Four loops cost n^4 steps. What if you combined the lists in pairs?
hints.pattern: Meet in the middle: hash map of all sums of the first two lists, then look up the negatives of sums of the other two.
hints.walkthrough: The condition a + b + c + d = 0 is the same as a + b = -(c + d). Count how many times each sum a + b occurs (n^2 pairs). Then for every pair (c, d), add the number of earlier pairs whose sum equals -(c + d). That is two double loops instead of one quadruple loop: O(n^2) time and O(n^2) space. With n up to 100 the answer is at most 10^8, which fits in an int.
